kb.label: The top five cities, ranked -- and what each one costs
kb.body: Ranked on 2 November 2026, after he asked for a top five. 1. Paris -- the only one he can land in without an offer, because the APS gives him a year and an employer converts rather than sponsors. 2. Dublin -- the Critical Skills Employment Permit qualifies on salary alone with no labour market test, it works in English, and Google, Meta, Microsoft, Stripe and Workday run EMEA from there; rent and weather are the cost. 3. Amsterdam -- the best of the three to live in and English-language workplaces are normal, but it is third because the zoekjaar probably does not cover an INSEAD degree, so the offer has to come first. 4. Singapore -- an INSEAD campus and a deep alumni base, English, the APAC seat for most Big Tech, a manageable Employment Pass, and the one market where his five years in South-East Asia read as an asset rather than something to explain. 5. Barcelona or Madrid -- in on the Spanish he will have and on leisure, out on Big Tech density, pay, and working Spanish being assumed outside MBB. Just outside: Brussels, which has the lowest salary bar of the group and moves up the moment permits become the binding constraint. Ruled out: Switzerland on the labour market test and quota, and Germany, the UK and the UAE by his own choice. Copenhagen is a company target rather than a city target -- Novo Nordisk, Maersk, Orsted and a short list of others hire in English, but INSEAD barely places in the Nordics and there is no job-search permit for a non-Danish graduate. The structural point behind the whole list: pick the employer first and the city follows, because a multinational moves people between its own offices far more easily than a new employer sponsors a stranger.
